About Mywarf 5mg Tablet

Mywarf 5mg Tablet is primarily used to prevent and treat deep vein thrombosis (blood clots in leg veins) and pulmonary embolism (blood clots in the lung) by reducing the formation of a blood clot. Deep vein thrombosis is a medical condition in which blood clots form in deep veins, usually in the legs. Pulmonary embolism is a condition in which blood clot blocks the arteries in the lungs.

Mywarf 5mg Tablet contains Warfarin, which works by inhibiting the production of clotting factors by decreasing the action of vitamin K. This prevents the conversion of fibrinogen (soluble protein) to fibrin (insoluble protein), thereby preventing blood clot formation.

Take Mywarf 5mg Tablet with or without food as advised by the doctor and swallow it as a whole with a glass of water. Do not crush, chew or break it. Your doctor will advise you on how often you take your tablets based on your medical condition. Some people may experience unusual bleeding or skin rash. Most of these side effects of Mywarf 5mg Tablet do not require medical attention and gradually resolve over time. However, if the side effects persist or worsen, please consult your doctor.

If you are known to be allergic to Mywarf 5mg Tablet or any other medicines, please tell your doctor. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, it is advised to consult a doctor before using Mywarf 5mg Tablet . If you have a stomach ulcer, kidney or liver problems, high blood pressure, or bleeding problems, inform your doctor before taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet . It would help if you had frequent INR (International Normalized Ratio) or prothrombin time tests to measure your blood clotting time, as Mywarf 5mg Tablet prolongs bleeding time. You must be cautious while shaving and brushing your teeth to avoid too much bleeding from the injury site.  

Uses of Mywarf 5mg Tablet

Mywarf 5mg Tablet used for the prevention of blood clots. The detailed uses of Mywarf 5mg Tablet are as follows:

  • Prevention of Blood Clots: Mywarf 5mg Tablet prevents the formation of blood clots in patients at risk of stroke, heart attack, or deep vein thrombosis, particularly in conditions like atrial fibrillation and rheumatic heart disease.
  • Treatment of Blood Clots: Mywarf 5mg Tablet treats existing blood clots and prevents them from growing or breaking loose in conditions like venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
  • Prosthetic Heart Valve Management: Mywarf 5mg Tablet prevents complications after prosthetic heart valve insertion by reducing the risk of blood clots.
  • Prevention of Transient Cerebral Ischaemic Attacks: Mywarf 5mg Tablet prevents transient cerebral ischaemic attacks (TIAs or mini-strokes).

Key Benefits

Mywarf 5mg Tablet belongs to a class of drugs known as anticoagulants or blood thinners. Mywarf 5mg Tablet is primarily used to prevent and treat deep vein thrombosis (blood clots in leg veins) and pulmonary embolism (blood clots in the lung) by reducing the formation of a blood clot. Mywarf 5mg Tablet works by inhibiting the production of clotting factors by decreasing the action of vitamin K. This prevents the conversion of fibrinogen (soluble protein) to fibrin (insoluble protein), thereby preventing blood clot formation.

Directions for Use

  • Mywarf 5mg Tablet can be taken with or without food.
  • It is recommended to take Mywarf 5mg Tablet once daily. However, your doctor may adjust the dosage and timing based on the prothrombin time/INR test ( a test used to measure the time it takes for your blood to clot).
  • Swallow Mywarf 5mg Tablet as a whole with a glass of water.
  • Do not crush, chew, or break it.

How Mywarf 5mg Tablet Works

Mywarf 5mg Tablet contains Warfarin, which works by inhibiting the production of clotting factors by decreasing the action of vitamin K. This prevents the conversion of fibrinogen (soluble protein) to fibrin (insoluble protein), thereby preventing blood clot formation.

Safety Advice

Alcohol

Unsafe

You are recommended to avoid consumption of alcohol with Mywarf 5mg Tablet as it may increase the risk of bleeding.

Pregnancy

Unsafe

Mywarf 5mg Tablet is a Category D pregnancy drug. It means Mywarf 5mg Tablet can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. It should not be given in pregnant women with mechanical heart valves as they are at high risk of thromboembolism.

Breast Feeding

Caution

Mywarf 5mg Tablet is not found in breast milk, but it should be used with caution if prescribed by your doctor.

Driving

Safe if prescribed

Mywarf 5mg Tablet usually does not affect your ability to drive or operate machinery.

Liver

Caution

Take Mywarf 5mg Tablet with caution, especially if you have a history of Liver diseases/conditions. The dose may be adjusted by your doctor as required.

Kidney

Caution

Take Mywarf 5mg Tablet with caution, especially if you have a history of Kidney diseases/conditions. The dose may be adjusted by your doctor as required.

Children

Consult your doctor

It is unknown whether Mywarf 5mg Tablet is safe and effective in children. So, please consult a doctor if you have any concerns regarding the use of Mywarf 5mg Tablet for children.

Heart

Safe if prescribed

Mywarf 5mg Tablet can be used in heart patients if prescribed by the physician to reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke. Please consult your physician if you have any concerns.

Geriatrics

Caution

Mywarf 5mg Tablet is generally safe for use in elderly patients if recommended by the physician.

What if I have taken an overdose of Mywarf 5mg Tablet

Do not take more than the prescribed dose of Mywarf 5mg Tablet as it may cause overdose resulting in excessive bleeding. If you suspect you have taken overdose or notice signs of overdose, please consult a doctor immediately.

Diet & Lifestyle Advise

  • Avoid making any changes in your diet without first talking to your doctor.

  • Opt for foods that are high in vitamin K (liver, leafy green vegetables, or vegetable oils) as Mywarf 5mg Tablet may lower Vitamin K in your body.

  • Cranberry juice, grapefruit juice, noni juice, and pomegranate juice may interact with Mywarf 5mg Tablet and lead to unwanted side effects. Hence try to avoid these juices while taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet .

  • Avoid drinking alcohol as it increases risk of gastrointestinal ulcer/bleeding.

Have a query?

Drug Warnings

Mywarf 5mg Tablet should be used with caution in children. Prolonged use of Mywarf 5mg Tablet may cause hair loss. Regular blood tests are recommended while taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet to check the time taken for your blood to clot and the level of platelets (blood cells). If you have a painful skin rash, inform your doctor immediately as it may be due to a serious condition called calciphylaxis (accumulation of calcium in small blood vessels of skin and fat tissues) which may cause painful skin ulcers, blood clots, and serious skin infections. Patients with chronic kidney disease are at high risk of getting calciphylaxis. If you have any high blood pressure, kidney, liver, or heart problems, please inform your doctor before taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet so that the dose may be adjusted accordingly. Mywarf 5mg Tablet may cause serious side effects and death of skin tissue (skin necrosis or gangrene). Call your doctor if you have pain, color, or temperature change in any area of your body or purple toes syndrome. Before undergoing any type of surgery tell your doctor that you are taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet . Your doctor might tell you to stop taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet . Mywarf 5mg Tablet is pregnancy category D medicine and can cause birth defects, or miscarriage. So, if you are pregnant or planning for pregnancy or are a nursing mother tell your doctor that you are taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet . Mywarf 5mg Tablet should be used with caution in patients with severe Anemia (low RBC count), malignancies (any cancer), and Trauma (injuries).

Drug-Drug Interactions

Login/Sign Up

WarfarinTamoxifen
Critical
How does the drug interact with Mywarf 5mg Tablet:
Taking tamoxifen with Mywarf 5mg Tablet can increase the risk of bleeding.

How to manage the interaction:
Taking Tamoxifen with Mywarf 5mg Tablet is not recommended but can be taken together if prescribed by a doctor. However, consult a doctor if you experience bleeding, vomiting, blood in your urine or stools, headache, dizziness, or weakness. Do not discontinue any medications without consulting a doctor.
WarfarinMiconazole
Severe
How does the drug interact with Mywarf 5mg Tablet:
Co-administration of Mywarf 5mg Tablet with miconazole may increase the risk of bleeding.

How to manage the interaction:
Although there is a possible interaction between miconazole and Mywarf 5mg Tablet, you can take these medicines together if prescribed by a doctor. However, if you experience unusual bleeding or bruising, dizziness, lightheadedness, red or black, tarry stools, coughing up or vomiting fresh or dried blood that looks like coffee grounds, severe headache, and weakness, consult a doctor immediately. Do not stop using medications without a doctor's advice.
WarfarinEdoxaban
Severe

Coadministration of Mywarf 5mg Tablet with Edoxaban can increase the risk of bleeding.

How to manage the interaction:
There may be a possible interaction between Edoxaban and Mywarf 5mg Tablet, but they can be taken together if a doctor has prescribed them. However, consult a doctor immediately if you experience unusual bleeding or bruising, vomiting, blood in your urine or stools, headache, dizziness, or weakness, contact a doctor. Do not discontinue any medications without consulting a doctor.

Coadministration of Mywarf 5mg Tablet with Piroxicam can increase the risk of bleeding.

How to manage the interaction:
Although taking Piroxicam with Mywarf 5mg Tablet together can result in an interaction, they can be taken together if prescribed by a doctor. However, if you experience unusual bleeding or bruising, vomiting, blood in your urine or stools, headache, dizziness, or weakness consult a doctor immediately. Do not stop using any medications without consulting a doctor.
WarfarinPhenobarbital
Severe
How does the drug interact with Mywarf 5mg Tablet:
Taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet with Phenobarbital can significantly lower the Mywarf 5mg Tablet blood levels.

How to manage the interaction:
Although taking phenobarbital and Mywarf 5mg Tablet together can result in an interaction, it can be taken if a doctor has prescribed it. However, if you observe any indications of blood clots, such as chest discomfort, shortness of breath, abrupt loss of vision, and/or pain, redness, or swelling in an extremity, consult a doctor. Do not stop using any medications without a doctor's advice.
WarfarinPentobarbital
Severe
How does the drug interact with Mywarf 5mg Tablet:
Taking Mywarf 5mg Tablet with Pentobarbital can reduce the blood levels of Mywarf 5mg Tablet, making it less effective.

How to manage the interaction:
Although taking Pentobarbital acid and Mywarf 5mg Tablet together can result in an interaction, they can be taken together if prescribed by a doctor. However, if you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden loss of vision, and/or pain, redness or swelling in an extremity, consult a doctor immediately. Do not stop using any medications without consulting a doctor.

Drug-Food Interactions

WARFARIN-5MGVitamin-K rich foods
Moderate
Common Foods to Avoid:
Avocado, Black Liquorice, Broccoli, Brussels Sprouts, Cabbage, Collard Greens, Coriander, Turnip Greens, Spinach, Green Tea, Kale

How to manage the interaction:
Increasing vitamin K levels in the body can promote clotting and reduce the effectiveness of Mywarf 5mg Tablet. Avoid or limit consumption of foods rich in vitamin K while being treated with Mywarf 5mg Tablet.

FAQs
